taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time. Cases: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth computed with zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through the time zones and dates.

**Step 1: Confirm the date**
Oct 24, 2026 is a Saturday. Six days later = Oct 30, 2026, which is indeed a Friday (matches the problem statement).

**Step 2: Determine PT offset on Oct 30, 2026**
US DST ends Nov 1, 2026 (first Sunday in November), so Oct 30 is still in **PDT (UTC-7)**.

11:59 PM PDT, Oct 30, 2026 = 23:59 UTC-7 → **06:59 UTC, Oct 31, 2026**.

**Step 3: Determine Madrid offset on Oct 31, 2026**
EU DST ends Oct 25, 2026 (last Sunday in October), so by Oct 30-31, Madrid is in **CET (UTC+1)**.

06:59 UTC + 1 hour = **07:59 CET, Oct 31, 2026**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Reasoning:
- Oct 30, 2026 is a Friday, so "this coming Monday" = November 2, 2026.
- EU DST ends on the last Sunday of October (Oct 25, 2026), so Madrid is already on CET (UTC+1) by Oct 30.
- US DST ends on the first Sunday of November (Nov 1, 2026), so by Nov 2, Los Angeles is on PST (UTC-8).
- Difference: CET (UTC+1) − PST (UTC−8) = 9 hours ahead.
- 10:00 AM PST + 9 hours = 7:00 PM CET.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts at 18:00 CEST (UTC+2) on Sat, Oct 24, 2026, which is 16:00 UTC.

Adding exactly 48 hours of elapsed time gives 16:00 UTC on Mon, Oct 26, 2026.

However, DST ends in Madrid on Sun, Oct 25, 2026 at 03:00 CEST → 02:00 CET (clocks go back one hour). So by Oct 26, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1), not CEST.

Converting 16:00 UTC on Oct 26 to Madrid time: 16:00 + 1 = 17:00 CET.

So although the clock reading advances by 48 hours nominally landing on 18:00, the actual 48-hour duration ends at 17:00 local time due to the autumn clock change.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Step 1: Determine the start time in UTC.**
October 26, 2026 is before the US ends Daylight Saving Time (which ends Nov 1, 2026), so PT = PDT = UTC-7.
10:00 AM PDT = 17:00 UTC on Oct 26, 2026.

**Step 2: Add 72 hours.**
17:00 UTC Oct 26 + 72 hours = 17:00 UTC Oct 29, 2026.
(Note: Pacific Time doesn't change during this window, so the PT equivalent stays 10:00 AM PDT.)

**Step 3: Convert to Madrid time.**
EU ends Daylight Saving Time on October 25, 2026 (last Sunday of October) — before our deadline. So by October 29, Madrid is on standard time, CET = UTC+1.
17:00 UTC + 1 hour = 18:00 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Submissions close: Oct 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. On that date the US is still on EDT (DST ends Nov 1, 2026), so ET = UTC‑4.

11:59 PM EDT Oct 31 → 03:59 UTC Nov 1, 2026.

Add 36 hours → 15:59 UTC Nov 2, 2026.

Madrid: Spain's DST ended Oct 25, 2026, so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1) by Nov 2.

15:59 UTC + 1h = 16:59 Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Converting the timestamp:**

1791788340 seconds since Unix epoch (1970‑01‑01 00:00:00 UTC):

- 1791788340 ÷ 86400 = 20738 days, remainder 25140 seconds.
- 25140 s = 06:59:00 (UTC time of day).
- Counting 20738 days from 1970‑01‑01 lands on **2026‑10‑11** (UTC date).

So the deadline is **2026‑10‑11 06:59:00 UTC**.

Tokyo uses JST (UTC+9), so add 9 hours:

06:59 UTC + 9:00 = 15:59 JST (same calendar day, since 6:59+9 < 24:00).

ANSWER: 2026-10-11 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z. On that date, Madrid (CEST, UTC+2) switches to standard time (CET, UTC+1) at 01:00 UTC (clocks go back at 03:00 CEST → 02:00 CET). Since 02:30 UTC falls after this transition, Madrid is already on CET (UTC+1).

02:30 UTC + 1 hour = 03:30 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25, 2026 (confirmed: Jan 1, 2026 is a Thursday → Oct 1, 2026 is also a Thursday → Sundays fall on Oct 4, 11, 18, 25).

**Pacific Time check:** On Oct 25, 2026, US DST is still in effect (ends Nov 1, 2026), so Pacific Time is UTC−7 (PDT).
11:59 PM PDT, Oct 25, 2026 → UTC: 23:59 + 7:00 = 06:59 UTC, Oct 26, 2026.

**Madrid Time check:** Spain's DST ends on the same day, Oct 25, 2026 (clocks fall back at 3:00 AM CEST → 2:00 AM CET). So by the time we reach 06:59 UTC on Oct 26, Madrid has already switched to standard time: CET = UTC+1.

06:59 UTC + 1:00 = 07:59 local time, Oct 26, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline falls on November 1, 2026, the day DST ends in the US (clocks fall back at 2:00 AM, so by noon Eastern Time is already EST, UTC-5). Lima, Peru stays at UTC-5 year-round (no DST), so Eastern Standard Time and Peru time are the same offset. Thus noon Eastern = noon in Lima, same calendar day.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) is defined as UTC−12. "December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE" is equivalent to January 1, 2027, 00:00 UTC−12.

Convert to UTC: add 12 hours → January 1, 2027, 12:00 UTC.
Convert to JST (UTC+9): add 9 hours → January 1, 2027, 21:00 JST.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney is in AEDT (UTC+11) by October 5, 2026 (DST begins Oct 4). New York is in EDT (UTC-4) at that time.

Convert: 17:00 Oct 5 AEDT → UTC: 17:00 − 11:00 = 06:00 UTC Oct 5.
UTC → EDT: 06:00 − 4:00 = 02:00 EDT Oct 5.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
